title: Knots across time are minimal decisive sets; pairwise memory is exactly the single ANDs and ORs
subject: What a process's states over time knot with, read with the canonical knot test on its space-time law
conclusion: Written as its space-time law, a deterministic process is a static law on its trajectories, and its knots joining a cell's value after T steps to the first row are exactly that value with the minimally decisive sets of two or more past cells: the sets that, set suitably, fix the future value while no smaller set does. A single deciding cell gives a tie. A nonconstant future value has no knot across time exactly when it is a single conjunction or disjunction of literals, so a process remembers its past only pairwise exactly then. A linear rule with polynomial p has one two-time knot per lag, the support of p^T plus the cell, with |supp p| + 1 places at every lag 2^k; through intermediate rows Ledrappier's law gives 2 + w(T) inside the light cone for T <= 6, and the least knot leaves the light cone at T = 7. In one step of Life the knots are the 70 sets of four neighbours, and the cell's own present is in none.
